description: An air operations officer must publish the next-day apron schedule for four routine rotary-wing support activities, assigning aircraft, setting work windows and locations, and recording the coordination actions needed to keep the schedule executable.

shared_context.S1: The available aircraft for tomorrow are H-17, H-22, H-23, and H-24.
shared_context.S2: Tomorrow's routine support requirements are one cargo shuttle to the depot, one navigation-proficiency sortie, one avionics ground-systems check, and one afternoon standby block.
shared_context.S3: Maj. Alvarez publishes the binding aircraft schedule, and each aircraft may be assigned to only one primary activity.
shared_context.S4: The draft planning board currently shows the cargo shuttle at 0800-1000, the avionics check at 0900-1100, the navigation sortie at 1300-1500, and the standby block at 1500-1700.
shared_context.S5: At the routine 1600 air-operations brief, the maintenance, weather, logistics, and flight-operations sections review their next-day updates before Maj. Alvarez publishes the schedule.

PF1.text: H-17 is the maintenance aircraft and is due for its scheduled 100-hour inspection, so it must remain in the maintenance bay from exactly 0800 to 1200; H-22 is the aircraft cleared to conduct the cargo shuttle instead. CW2 Mercer confirmed the inspection status during the morning maintenance review, but the aircraft-status board has not yet been updated.

PF2.text: A confirmed low-ceiling and crosswind period is forecast over the north apron from 1300 to 1500, so the navigation-proficiency sortie must run from 0900 to 1100 at the south apron. Lt. Okafor received the updated aviation forecast at midday, but it is not yet on the afternoon planning board.

PF3.text: The fuel bowser is booked to service H-23 from exactly 1500 to 1530 tomorrow, and that aircraft must be parked at the fuel point during that interval. SFC Patel received the confirmed bowser appointment from the support company this morning, but the appointment has not been entered on the apron schedule.

PF4.text: Cpl. Duran is the only available crew coordinator tomorrow with current certification for the cargo shuttle's external-load inspection, so Duran must be assigned to the cargo shuttle. The certification was renewed in the personnel tracker this morning, but the updated qualification roster has not yet been circulated to air operations.

acceptance_conditions: H-22 must be assigned to the cargo shuttle.
H-17 must be assigned to the maintenance inspection from 0800-1200.
The navigation-proficiency sortie must run from 0900-1100 at the south apron.
H-23's fuel-point servicing window must be recorded as 1500-1530.
Cpl. Duran must be assigned as the cargo-shuttle coordinator.
The schedule must include maintenance, weather, fuel, and cargo-coordinator coordination actions.
The cargo qualification fact must be cited as justification.

content_checks.C6: 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF3' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF4' in justification_fact_ids and decisions['cargo_aircraft'] == 'H-22' and decisions['maintenance_window'] == '0800-1200' and decisions['navigation_window'] == '0900-1100' and 'south' in decisions['navigation_apron'] and decisions['fuel_point_window'] == '1500-1530' and 'Duran' in decisions['cargo_coordinator']

decisive_facts.why: H-17 is explicitly the maintenance aircraft for exactly 0800-1200, while H-22 is the aircraft cleared for the cargo shuttle, changing both aircraft assignments and the maintenance window.
The 1300-1500 north-apron weather restriction changes the navigation sortie to exactly 0900-1100 at the south apron.
The confirmed H-23 bowser appointment fixes the fuel-point servicing window at exactly 1500-1530.
Duran's unique current external-load certification changes the cargo coordinator assignment to exactly Cpl. Duran and supplies the fact that must be cited.
